author: Forbes
description:
Kate McLeod’s home office is part workspace, part creative sanctuary and part living scrapbook.

The founder invites Forbes Vetted inside her New York City home, from the light-filled room where she works surrounded by crystals, cookbooks and family keepsakes to the kitchen where an experiment with cocoa butter became the Body Stone.

Kate also opens up about the woman who changed the course of her life, her unexpected journey from finance to pastry school to entrepreneurship, and what she learned watching her husband, Hinge founder Justin McLeod, keep going when the company nearly failed.

Step inside the deeply personal spaces, objects and stories that shape how Kate McLeod creates, works and lives.

0:00 Inside Kate McLeod’s Home Office
1:09 The Symbols Built Into Her Workspace
2:08 The Person Who Changed Her Life
3:13 The Books, Crystals and Objects She Collects
4:04 Why Her Kids’ Art Is Priceless
5:30 The Message She Looks at Every Day
6:28 The Kitchen Where the Body Stone Began
title: Crystals, Cookbooks And Creativity: Inside Kate McLeod’s Home

author: Forbes
description:
Jennifer Hyman is perhaps best known as the cofounder and former CEO of Rent-the-Runway, the company that virtually created the on-demand clothing rental category. Hyman left Rent the Runway earlier this year, at the time saying only that her next step would be to “help women feel and do all of the things that they want to accomplish.” 

Today, we have a firsthand look at what exactly that next step is: Hyman will take the helm of Babylist, the $750 million (revenue) baby registry business. Hyman joined ForbesWomen editor Maggie McGrath to discuss the move.

author: Forbes
description:
After signing a lucrative new talk show contract with Spotify and Netflix, wellness-creator-turned-entertainment-mogul Jay Shetty has big business plans and Hollywood aspirations.

IfJay Shetty was going to level up his podcast, he figured he needed to upgrade the studio in which he records it. So before his seven-year-old show, 'On Purpose,' relaunched this month on Netflix, the 38-year-old self-help guru says he spent around $500,000 to renovate the space with specific colors and custom artwork (such asincluding a piece of glass covered in bubble wrap) to evoke the kind of vulnerability and fragility he hopes to encourage from his guests.

Sitting inside his sprawling Hollywood Hills home, worth an estimated $8 million, Shetty’s digs are a far cry from the Hindu monk principles of humble detachment he once practiced and has encouraged to display. title: How Jay Shetty Went From Monk To Media Mogul
